name: EM3-1-the-wall-is-a-stroke-per-chain

name: EM3-2-the-wall-thins-to-nothing

name: EM3-3-the-wash-is-a-second-outline
note: Two outlines over one room double every shared wall.

name: EM3-5-the-wash-is-a-rect-a-cell
old: while (gx + run < occ.w && occ.at(gx + run, gz)) run++;
note: A fillRect a cell shows its own grid at this alpha.

name: EM3-6-the-caret-points-south
note: The motor measures yaw from -Z; a plan lays z down the paper.

name: EM3-7-the-caret-scales-with-the-zoom
old: ctx.moveTo(x + hx * CARET_R, y + hy * CARET_R);
new: ctx.moveTo(x + hx * CARET_R * 0.2, y + hy * CARET_R * 0.2);

name: EM3-8-the-caret-is-filled-before-its-halo
note: A halo over the ink it carries is a halo that hides it.

name: EM3-11-the-floor-strip-is-TOP-storey-at-the-bottom

name: EM3-12-the-floor-strip-is-centred-down-the-edge-again
new:
const rowsTotal = shown.length * rowH + Math.max(0, shown.length - 1) * gap;
  const top = Math.max(padY, ((opts.paperH ?? 400) - rowsTotal) / 2);
note: THE DEFECT THE BROWSER PROBE SAW, put back: centred down the right edge, "Floor 1" lands squarely under the right gauntlet. The paper's rectangle is not the part of it a player can SEE.

name: EM3-15-the-sheet-derives-its-storeys-from-what-was-REVEALED
old:
const rows = model?.rows ?? [];
    if (frame && frame.rows === rows) return frame;
new:
const rows = (model?.rows ?? []).filter((r) => rec()?.revealed?.has(r.key));
    if (frame && frame.rows === rows) return frame;
note: Then the map renumbers itself as the player explores, and the frame slides under the caret.

name: EM3-16-the-frame-is-keyed-on-the-model-WRAPPER
note: A host that hands a fresh bag back per call re-derives every triangle in the level, every frame.

name: EM3-17-the-sheet-draws-in-WORLD-units-rather-than-plan-units
old: for (const chain of plan.chains) for (const p of chain) { p.x -= f.origin[0]; p.y -= f.origin[1]; }
note: The window's clamp wants a map that starts at (0,0); a dungeon sits wherever its blocks were laid.

name: EM3-18-a-building-keeps-a-prior-run-tier
note: DFU's always-colour law: a building has no grayscale tier at all (AutomapModel.cs:46-72).

name: EM3-19-the-static-key-reads-the-CACHE
note: A storey change drops the cache, so the key answers 'none' and the kept ink layer shows the old storey.

name: EM3-20-the-two-passes-do-not-share-a-grid
note: The wash then sits beside its own walls rather than inside them.

name: EM3-21-a-mark-is-drawn-on-every-storey
note: A note sits 0.7 off whatever surface it was stuck to; it belongs to the storey nearest its height.

name: EM3-22-the-caret-is-drawn-on-a-floor-the-player-is-not-on
note: A lie the 3D map could not tell.

name: EM3-25-the-floor-keys-take-the-arrows
why: The unit pins drive `step` and `key` directly rather than through the window's pan ladder, so none of them can fail this. IT IS COVERED, by tools/enhancedMapProbe.mjs: "THE ARROWS PAN, they do not change storey" presses ArrowRight on a zoomed automap sheet and asserts the storey held while the view moved.

name: EM4-1-a-ground-flat-is-a-building
note: THE DEFECT A PIN FOUND, put back: 0xfb is in SHOWALL, so every patch of scenery draws as architecture.

name: EM4-2-a-house-is-washed-like-a-shop
old: export const isEnterable = (byte) => { const q = quarterOf(byte); return q !== null && q !== 'house'; };

name: EM4-3-the-street-is-built-up
note: Then the whole town is one solid block and there is no plan at all.

name: EM4-4-the-field-disagrees-with-the-anchors-across-blocks
new: const dst = (h - 1 - (by + BLOCK_PX - 1 - y)) * w + bx;
note: The shipped map's own two flips, which mirror the plan against the names when the two are drawn as one picture.

name: EM4-5-the-block-rows-run-the-other-way
new: const dst = (by + BLOCK_PX - 1 - y) * w + bx;

name: EM4-6-a-block-off-its-own-grid-writes-past-the-field
old: if (bx < 0 || by < 0 || bx + BLOCK_PX > w || by + BLOCK_PX > h) continue;   // a block off its own grid

name: EM4-7-the-reader-is-unbounded
old: return (x, y) => (x >= 0 && y >= 0 && x < field.w && y < field.h) && pick(field.bytes[y * field.w + x]);
note: boundarySegments walks one past the edge on every side; an unbounded reader wraps a row.

name: EM4-8-the-wash-goes-over-the-wall
EM4-11-a-discovered-residence-is-named-without-a-quest
note: A home you have found is still nobody's business - the shipped map's own ladder.

name: EM4-13-an-undiscovered-building-is-named
note: The map would hand the player every shop in the city before they had walked a street.

name: EM4-14-an-undiscovered-quest-residence-is-rung
note: The map would give the quest away before the player had found the door.

old: const base = Math.max(NAME_SIZE_MIN, Math.min(NAME_SIZE_MAX, NAME_SIZE * Math.sqrt(view.scale)));

name: EM4-17-the-names-are-laid-at-a-whole-town-fit
note: At a fit they are a grey band rather than words, and the solver's work is spent for nothing.

name: EM4-19-the-plates-are-laid-again-every-frame
note: The collision solver is the most expensive thing this sheet does and the view moves far more often than the town.

name: EM4-20-a-plate-the-solver-gave-up-on-is-drawn-anyway
old: if (!s || s.replaced) return;   // the solver gave up on it
why: The unit fixtures never overrun the collision solver's three iterations, so no plate comes back `replaced`. IT IS COVERED, by tools/enhancedMapProbe.mjs, which lays a nine-block town of twelve named buildings and counts the plates that survive at two zooms.

name: EM4-21-the-travel-tag-is-asserted-rather-than-derived
note: The world host reads it to know a TRAVEL map is up; a crypt's plan is not a thing you can travel from.

name: EM4-22-a-sheet-is-never-told-it-went-DOWN
why: EM1's world sheet is the only one that claims chrome, and the unit pins drive the switch with a stub sheet that claims none - so nothing is left showing for them to notice. IT IS COVERED, by tools/enhancedMapProbe.mjs: three checks walk a town sheet to the bay and back and assert the search box is hidden, then shown, then hidden again.

name: EM7-1-two-quarters-become-one
note: The whole point of four colours is that four things look different.

name: EM7-2-the-plus-one-drifts
old: export const quarterOfType = (type) => (type == null ? null : quarterOf(type + 1));
new: export const quarterOfType = (type) => (type == null ? null : quarterOf(type));
note: A summary's type is the grid's byte MINUS one. Lose that and every name is lettered as the quarter next door.

name: EM7-3-the-wash-is-a-fill
note: Opaque, the parchment stops reading through and the sheet is a sticker again.

name: EM7-4-the-name-ink-is-raw-paint
note: Unmixed, a name is classic's flat blue on parchment rather than ink with a hue.

name: EM7-5-the-static-key-forgets-the-quarters
note: EM3's own lesson on the other sheet: a key that does not name what is inked keeps an old wash under a new outline.

name: EM8-1-the-tick-marks-the-words-not-the-building
note: Then the tick says nothing the words did not already say, and says it in the wrong place.

name: EM8-2-every-plate-gets-a-leader
note: A line under every name in a dense quarter is the smear the solver exists to prevent.

name: EM8-3-no-plate-ever-gets-a-leader
note: A displaced plate then floats over a building it does not name, which is the lie EM8 was written to stop.

name: EM8-4-the-weight-is-applied-inside-the-clamp
old:
const base = Math.max(NAME_SIZE_MIN, Math.min(NAME_SIZE_MAX, NAME_SIZE * Math.sqrt(view.scale)));
    return base * weight;
new: return Math.max(NAME_SIZE_MIN, Math.min(NAME_SIZE_MAX, NAME_SIZE * Math.sqrt(view.scale) * weight));
note: THE DEFECT THE PINS FOUND, put back: past scale 2.4 every plate is already at NAME_SIZE_MAX, so a landmark and the shop beside it come out identical exactly where the map is most read.

name: EM8-5-a-quest-loses-its-pen-to-its-quarter
note: A quest is why the map is open at all; it outranks knowing the building is somebody's house.
